To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

chronic alcohol consumption in mice results in a reduction of alcohol metabolism and a reduction of the hepatic expression of liver alcohol dehydroge-nases (ADH) 1 and ADH2, which results in a significant increase in the plasma levels of alcohol and acetaldehyde.
CAC is associated with an increase in the systemic exposure to alcohol and its metabolites, and that the increased systemic exposure is associated with an increased activity of hepatic ADH3.
chronic alcohol consumption in mice is associated with an increase in alcohol clearance rate, a decrease in blood alcohol concentration, and an increase in the volume of distribution of alcohol.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new methods of analysis of organic compounds in the environment.
the metabolic pharmacokinetic effects of chronic alcohol consumption mediated via the liver alcohol dehydrogenses 1 and 4 in mice.
the role of the alcohol dehydrogenase isoenzymes in ethanol metabolism and their possible role in the development of the tolerance and dependence syndrome in the rat and mouse.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the metabolic pharmacokinetic of CAC is mediated by liver ADH1/3, which are responsible for the systemic alcohol metabolism.
ADH1 and 3 play an important role in the metabolic pharmacokinetic of CAC in mice.
ADH1 and/or ADH3 contribute to the metabolic pharmacology of chronic alcohol consumption.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the metabolic pharmacokinetic parameters of CAC are altered by ADH1 and/or ADH3.
ADH3 is a more important enzyme for alcohol metabolism during CAC than during acute alcohol consumption (AAC).
the liver is the major site of alcohol metabolism in mice and that ADH1 and 3 have distinct roles in alcohol metabolism in the liver.
The main takeaway from our work is that
liver ADH3 is responsible for the majority of the alcohol metabolism in the liver.
liver ADH1/ADH3 play a critical role in the metabolic pharmacokinetic profile of chronic alcohol consumption in mice.
ADH1 and 3 have opposing roles in the metabolism of alcohol, with ADH3 contributing to the maintenance of blood alcohol levels and ADH1 contributing to the clearance of blood alcohol.
